id: qc-03
title: Photonic sampling
paper: Zhong et al., Quantum computational advantage using photons (Jiuzhang) (arXiv Dec 2020; Science 370, 1460, 2020)
link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.01625
type: Benchmark
cutoff: 2020-12-03
domain: qc
profile: advantage

## expected_verdict
Conditional limitation. The experiment is real. But its validation tests (thermal, distinguishable, uniform hypotheses; two-point correlations; HOG) can be passed by a cheap classical sampler: Villalonga et al. beat it on total variation distance and KL divergence using low-order marginals. This weakens what the tests certify. It does not refute the hardness of exact or ideal GBS.

## I0
Can a photonic sampler generate a specified Gaussian-boson distribution beyond classical rates?

## evidence
- Setup: 50 single-mode squeezed-state inputs (as 25 two-mode squeezed sources) into a 100-mode ultralow-loss, fully connected, random interferometer; 100 SNSPD detectors; phase-locked; non-programmable unitary.
- Output: up to 76 photon clicks; state space ~10^30; in 200 s, 3,097,810 events at 43 clicks (the most common click number).
- Cost claim: sampling rate ~10^14 faster than supercomputers; TaihuLight (Fugaku) would need 8×10^16 s (2×10^16 s) = 2.5 (0.6) billion years to match 200 s of samples.
- Validation: likelihood-ratio tests against thermal, distinguishable-photon and uniform hypotheses; two-point correlation comparison; heavy-output generation (HOG); no full-distribution verification at high click numbers.

## intake
- Scope: (A) the device samples a GBS distribution close to ideal; (B) no classical algorithm can produce comparable samples in feasible time.
- Regime: 100 modes, threshold detectors, realistic loss, ~40–76 clicks; a fixed interferometer.
- Assumptions: passing the chosen tests implies closeness to ideal GBS; the best classical method is exact-probability (hafnian/Torontonian) sampling.
- Falsifiers: a polynomial-time classical sampler that passes the same tests or is closer to ideal in TVD/KL than the experiment.

## screen
- Must flag: the tests only rule out specific null hypotheses (thermal, distinguishable, uniform), not all efficient classical models; losses push toward classically simulable regimes; the cost estimate assumes exact simulation.
- Must request: comparison against low-order-marginal and loss-aware approximate samplers.

## retrieval
- Pre-cutoff must-finds: Aaronson & Arkhipov boson sampling; Hamilton et al. GBS; Torontonian / threshold-detector GBS (Quesada et al.); TaihuLight benchmark (Li et al.); Bayesian validation (Bentivegna et al.); lossy boson sampling (Brod & Aaronson); classical samplers beating near-term devices (Neville et al.).
- Current mode: Villalonga et al. 2021: k-th order marginal (Ursell function) approximations, cost quadratic in modes, better TVD and KL than the experiments; does not apply to random circuit sampling. Author "L. Li" overlap is a name collision (Google vs USTC).

## designer
- Compare experiment vs classical approximate samplers (orders 0–3, loss-aware) on held-out statistics: TVD/KL where computable, higher-order correlations, at equal sample counts and cost.

## champion
- Villalonga et al.'s second-order Boltzmann-machine / greedy marginal sampler, plus thermal and squashed-state models.

## panel
- Flaw: validation tests are spoofable. Repair: state advantage only relative to exact simulation; add tests that low-order models fail.

## run
- Public samples: recompute two-point correlations and run a second-order marginal sampler on a subset of modes; full 100-mode probabilities are out of scope.

## verdict
- Label: Conditional limitation: the claim licensed by these tests is weakened; exact-sampling hardness unaffected.
- Must say: spoofing the benchmark ≠ refuting the complexity-theoretic hardness of ideal GBS.
- Must not say: quantum advantage with photons is refuted; or the 2.5-billion-year figure is established.

## audit
- Check: 100 modes, 76 clicks, 200 s, 2.5 / 0.6 billion years; Villalonga et al. cost quadratic in modes; the L. Li collision.

## variants
- Validation statistics that discriminate against k-th order marginal models (high-order Ursell functions with adequate precision), or programmable interferometers with lower loss.
